title: Sebastian Raschka posts 11 hours on building a reasoning model
friendlyTitle: Sebastian Raschka has posted 11 hours on building a reasoning model
summary: Sebastian Raschka has posted eight coding lectures, more than 11 hours, on building a reasoning model from a small pretrained Qwen3 in Python and PyTorch. The series covers evaluation, inference-time scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation. He says the early text-generation examples can run on a CPU, and that later training is much more practical with a GPU. The post was on the front page of Hacker News today.
friendlySummary: Sebastian Raschka has posted eight coding lectures, more than 11 hours, on building a reasoning model from a small pretrained Qwen3 model in Python and PyTorch. The series covers how to test the model, how to spend more compute at answer time, reinforcement learning, and distillation. He says the early text examples can run on a normal processor, and that later training is much more practical with a graphics card. The post was on the front page of Hacker News today.
whyItMatters: If you use a reasoning model every day and have never seen the training loop, this is the long version of how the extra thinking is actually added. Raschka's frame is useful on its own: the model is the engine, and the agent harness is the machinery around it. You do not need the companion book to start the videos. You do need enough Python and PyTorch to follow the code, or the hours will be a tour rather than a build.
